nodes.question: B01_Q07
nodes.need: the surface area of the tower
nodes.hint: Surface › Analysis. Area works on curves, surfaces and solids. Watch for: Set Total twist to 0: the area drops, because twisting stretches the skin.
nodes.correct: Area measures the tower's envelope in square feet and finds its centroid. The Panel shows the number.
nodes.stage: Check your result: A number that proves the mass is right. Read outputs as data, not just as a picture. Area gives the surface area (sf) and the centroid.

wrong.volume: Volume would be a good check too, but this step reads the envelope area.
wrong.*: This step needs the surface area of the solid.

nodes.question: B01_Q06
nodes.need: a closed solid: lids on the loft's open top and bottom
nodes.hint: Surface › Util. The loft is a tube with two flat openings. Watch for: Only flat (planar) openings can be capped.
nodes.correct: Cap Holes fills the planar openings at the top and bottom, turning the lofted tube into a closed solid.
nodes.stage: Close the mass: A closed solid (Brep): the tower mass. Loft leaves the top and bottom open; Cap Holes adds flat lids to planar openings.

wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces would make loose discs, not one joined solid.
wrong.brepJoin: Brep Join joins existing pieces: there are no lids yet to join.
wrong.*: This step needs to close the loft's openings.

nodes.question: B01_Q05
nodes.need: a surface skinned from the base outline up to the twisted top
nodes.hint: Surface › Freeform. It takes a list of section curves. Watch for: Curves out of order make the skin fold back on itself.
nodes.correct: Loft skins a surface through the section curves in order. Both outlines go into the same C input, which merges them into one list.
nodes.stage: Skin between the profiles: One surface from the base outline to the twisted top. Loft builds a surface through section curves, in the order they arrive: base first, then top.

wrong.extrude: Extrude pushes one curve along a vector: it can't connect different profiles.
wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces only fills flat outlines: you'd get separate floor discs.
wrong.sweep1: Sweep1 needs a rail curve to follow. Here there are only section curves.
wrong.*: This step needs a surface through section curves.

nodes.question: B01_Q03
nodes.need: a transform that lifts the top outline along the up vector
nodes.hint: Transform › Euclidean. Geometry in, a Motion vector in.
nodes.correct: Move translates geometry along a vector. The top outline is copied up to roof height and the original stays on the ground.
nodes.stage: Copy the profile to the top: The top outline sitting at roof height. Transforms output a moved copy: the original stays where it was.

wrong.rotate: Rotate turns geometry in place: you'll need it next, but first the outline has to go up.
wrong.scale: Scale resizes around a point: the outline would stay on the ground.
wrong.*: This step needs a transform that shifts geometry along a vector.

nodes.question: B01_Q01
nodes.need: the total tower height: Floors × Floor-to-floor
nodes.hint: Maths › Operators. Two numbers in, their product out. Watch for: Don't type the height in by hand: it has to update whenever a slider moves.
nodes.correct: Multiplication turns two sliders into one derived value: 30 floors × 13 ft = 390 ft. Deriving values instead of typing them keeps the definition parametric.
nodes.stage: How tall is the tower?: One number: the total height in feet. Derive values from sliders: Floors × Floor-to-floor.

wrong.addition: Addition gives 30 + 13 = 43 ft, not the height of 30 stacked floors.
wrong.power: Power raises A to the B-th power: far too tall.
wrong.*: This step needs the product of two numbers.

nodes.question: B01_Q04
nodes.need: a transform that turns the lifted outline by the twist angle
nodes.hint: Transform › Euclidean. Geometry, Angle, and a Plane to turn around. Watch for: Angle is in radians unless the A input is set to Degrees (right-click A > Degrees).
nodes.correct: Rotate turns the lifted outline around the tower's centre. Degrees is switched on, so the Total twist slider reads −180° to 180°.
nodes.stage: Twist the top: The roof outline turned by the twist angle. A rotation needs a centre (the tower's centre point) and an angle.

wrong.move: Move shifts geometry. The outline has to turn, not shift.
wrong.mirror: Mirror flips across a plane: a jump, not a gradual twist.
wrong.orient: Orient maps geometry from one plane to another: much more set-up than a simple turn.
wrong.*: This step needs a transform that turns geometry by an angle.

nodes.question: B01_Q02
nodes.need: a vector pointing straight up, as long as the tower is tall
nodes.hint: Vector › Vector. Up is the Z axis; the Factor input sets the length. Watch for: Unit X and Unit Y point sideways.
nodes.correct: Unit Z makes a vector up the Z axis. Feeding the height into its Factor makes it exactly as long as the tower is tall.
nodes.stage: Point it upward: A vector straight up, as long as the tower is tall. A vector is a direction × a length. Unit Z gives the direction; its Factor sets the length.

wrong.unitX: Unit X points sideways along X: the top would slide off to the side.
wrong.unitY: Unit Y points sideways along Y: the top would slide off to the side.
wrong.vectorXYZ: Vector XYZ could do it, but needs X, Y and Z: Unit Z only needs the length.
wrong.*: This step needs a vector pointing straight up.

check.prompt: Which input of Move takes the up vector?
check.hint: G = geometry to move, T = the motion vector.
check.correct: T is the motion. Until it was connected Move used its default (10 units up); now the top sits at roof height.

wrong.G: G is the geometry to move: the top outline is already plugged in there.
wrong.*: That input isn't the motion vector.

check.prompt: The twist angle goes into which input of Rotate?
check.hint: G = geometry, A = angle, P = plane (the centre) to rotate around.
check.correct: A is the angle, read in degrees because Degrees is switched on.

wrong.G: G is the geometry: the outline is already connected.
wrong.P: P is the rotation plane: the centre point goes there.

check.prompt: The centre point goes into which input of Rotate?
check.hint: A rotation needs a centre to turn around.
check.correct: P is the plane to rotate around: a point there means 'turn around this point'.

wrong.A: A is the angle: that's the twist value.
wrong.*: That input isn't the centre of rotation.
